questions.q: In whose ways did Ahaziah walk because of the advice of his mother?
questions.a: Ahaziah walked in the ways of the house of Ahab, for his mother was his adviser in doing wicked things.

questions.q: How did Ahaziah act in Yahweh’s sight, as the house of Ahab was doing?
questions.a: Ahaziah did what was evil in Yahweh’s sight, as the house of Ahab was doing.

questions.q: Why did Ahaziah go to visit Joram, the son of Ahab?
questions.a: Ahaziah went down to Jezreel to see him because Joram had been wounded.

questions.q: What did God bring about through Ahaziah’s visit to Joram?
questions.a: The destruction of Ahaziah was brought about by God through his visit to Joram.

questions.q: What did Jehu recall of Ahaziah’s father?
questions.a: Jehu said that Ahaziah was a son of Jehoshaphat, who sought Yahweh with all his heart.

questions.q: What did Ahaziah’s mother do when she saw that he was dead?
questions.a: When she saw that her son was dead, she arose and killed all the royal children in the house of Judah.

questions.q: How long was Joash hidden in the house of God while Athaliah reigned?
questions.a: Joash was hidden in the house of God for six years while Athaliah reigned over the land.

commentary.text: The reign of Ahaziah, Athaliah destroys the royal family.

—The counsel of the ungodly ruins many young persons when they are setting out in the world. Ahaziah gave himself up to be led by evil men. Those who advise us to do wickedly, counsel us to our destruction; while they pretend to be friends, they are our worst enemies. See and dread the mischief of bad company. If not the infection, yet let the destruction be feared, Re 18:4. We have here, a wicked woman endeavouring to destroy the house of David, and a good woman preserving it. No word of God shall fall to the ground. The whole truth of the prophecies that the Messiah was to come from David, and thereby the salvation of the world, appeared to be now hung upon the brittle thread of the life of a single infant, to destroy whom was the interest of the reigning power. But God had purposed, and vain were the efforts of earth and hell.
